sentences.text: Fossils from Scotland reveal an eel-shaped creature measuring up to 6 cm in length.
The skull was made of hardened cartilage and included nasal and auditory capsules, a gill apparatus, and ambiguous jaw structures.
A fossilized braincase of P. australis showed the animal lacked a postorbital process and an intracranial joint.
The genus Palaeospondylus was first described by Traquair in 1890.
Remains of this genus have been found in Scotland and Australia.
In 2004, researchers suggested that Palaeospondylus was a larval lungfish.
A 2017 study proposed that Palaeospondylus was a stem chondrichthyan.
The Paleobi Database classifies Palaeospondylus under the class Chondrichthyes.
Fossils of Palaeospondylus date to the Early and Middle Devonian periods, living approximately 400 to 390 million years ago.
